order_reconstruction_rule.rule: GROUP BY (user_id, user_session, event_time) on event_type='purchase' rows
order_reconstruction_rule.certified_because: 98.1% of multi-purchase-row sessions share one identical purchase timestamp across all their purchase rows; session-only grouping (Rule A) produces implausible order spans (max observed ~full dataset window) due to session-ID reuse documented in Section 7.
order_reconstruction_rule.rejected_alternative: one order per user_session (ignores possible multiple checkout events within one reused/long-lived session id)

retention_horizon.primary_reason: Only horizon with a full-cohort-trustworthy trailing window for nearly the entire dataset (Oct/Nov/Dec cohorts fully covered, Jan cohort nearly covered).

churn_threshold_candidates_days.note: Candidates only -- nb03 must still validate FP rate and recall against future behavior.

superseded.reason_superseded: Pooling weights frequent repeat-buyers more heavily, biasing every percentile down by roughly 15-20%. Kept here only for audit trail.

nb03_status.median_22.0: validated, rejected (J too low, flags 77% of the base)
nb03_status.p95_87.3: NOT VALIDATABLE -- dropped on window arithmetic, never scored

known_limitations: user_id is cookie-scoped, not account-scoped -- every repeat-purchase/retention figure is a LOWER BOUND on true customer-level behavior.
category_code is null for ~98% of events -- use category_id for category-level grouping.
brand is null for ~42% of events.

Bot exclusion IS defined and applied project-wide since 01: sessions per active day (distinct user_session count / distinct active-day count) > 29.0 (1,605 users, 1.743% of events). Inherit it from handoff_params.json bot_exclusion; do not re-derive.

The order-size tail is NOT bot-driven (00's claim, disproved in 01) and is not an anomaly: 143 reseller/B2B-like bulk buyers (median ~130 distinct products over ~31 categories at a BELOW-average unit price). Kept and flagged as is_bulk_buyer in data/processed/cohort_assignments.parquet; exclude from MEAN-based monetary metrics in 04/05, report medians as headline.

DuckDB determinism: never reference row_number() OVER () through a lazy view (it is re-assigned per reference and corrupts joins -- this silently broke 01's first two commits), and never use approx_quantile for a reported figure. See src/data.py connect().
01's 4-type cart-abandonment decomposition is partial: 02 Section 0A splits the 48% residual, promoting `substitution` to a named type and leaving only `returned_browsed_only` unclassified.

OUTCOME LEAKAGE: the abandonment-type ranking in 01 Section 4 and 02 Section 0A is NOT a valid effect size -- the types' definitions reference purchases that can fall in the outcome window. 02 Section 0E re-tests with disjoint windows: deferred_intent collapses from OR 10.81 to 0.78 and the ranking inverts. Only abandonment VOLUME survives. nb05 must not build features from those types -- see leakage_rules_for_05.
The 'promo' cohort is a BLACK FRIDAY cohort: all detected discount-spike days fall in one week, so promo-vs-organic results are about a single trading event, not about discounting in general.

SPINE-1 FALSIFIED: behaviour (first-session depth) does NOT beat first-order value for predicting repeat purchase (D30 dead heat, value ahead at D60/D90) and both are weak (V~0.09-0.13). See spine_hypothesis_status; CLAUDE.md's spine has been revised accordingly.

CHURN THRESHOLD CERTIFIED: 42.2 days of purchase silence (P75 of per-user-median inter-purchase gaps), validated at flag date 2020-01-04 with FP rate 10.12% and recall 53.09% (Spec B). Inherit it from handoff_params.json churn_definition; do not re-derive or round it.
P95 CHURN CANDIDATE (87.3d) WAS NEVER TESTED and must not be cited as validated: it needs 2K=174.6 days of span against 152.0 available, so zero users can be scored against it.

D30 CANNOT MEASURE CHURN: under the certified 42.2d rule no user is churned before day 42.2, so 06's repeat_purchase_30d target is a REPEAT-PURCHASE target and must never be labelled churn. The shortest horizon that can carry a churn label is D43.

CHURN-THRESHOLD FLAG-DATE INSTABILITY: the J-optimal threshold drifts 43.5d -> 29.4d as the flag date moves 21 days earlier, tracking the shrinking lookback cap (95.1d -> 74.1d). This is left censoring in a 5-month window, not behaviour. Treat 42.2d as the centre of a 30-45d region; ~9 months of history would settle it.

ABANDONMENT-VOLUME SIGNAL IS ANCHOR-SENSITIVE: log1p(n_removals) holds at OR 1.37-1.44 for first-order-anchored outcomes at every churn threshold, but falls to 1.03-1.14 for a calendar-anchored churn label. 05 must carry time-since-first-order alongside it rather than expecting OR=1.38.

CHURN IS FIRST-PURCHASE CHURN: 88% of users flagged by the certified rule had exactly one order, vs 80% of the base. 04's at-risk cells and 08's intervention are activation problems (get a 2nd order), not win-back problems.

CHURN BASE RATE IS NOT RETENTION: 03's 84.84% true-churn base is a point-in-time STOCK measure on a calendar anchor; 02's 21.08% D60 retention is a FLOW measure anchored on each user's first order. Both are correct and they must never be quoted against each other. 03 Section 9A reproduces 02 exactly on the same users once the anchor is matched.

CHURN RULE RECALL IS 53%: the certified rule flags 36,495 users but the true at-risk base is 61,787. 08/09 must NOT treat flagged-population as at-risk-population -- every reach or ROI denominator built on the flagged count must be divided by recall (53.09%). All 28,986 missed churners sit BELOW the 42.2d threshold (median recency 23.7d).

CHURN THRESHOLD IS NOT IDENTIFIED: 42.2d is the centre of a 30-45d region; two independent methods agree there, but the estimate is robust to neither flag-date position nor cost asymmetry. ~9 months of history would identify it. Quote certified_region_days [30, 45], not the decimal; use 42.2d as the OPERATING value so 04/05/06 stay comparable.

FLOAT AGGREGATES ARE NOT REPRODUCIBLE WITHOUT ROUNDING (found in 04, applies project-wide): DuckDB's parallel avg()/sum() reduce in physical scan order, so brand_entropy, category_entropy, mean_price_pct_viewed and mean_intersession_gap_d differ across two evaluations of the same query in one session (order 20-30k rows, max |diff| ~9e-15), AND fetchdf() returns rows in an unstable parallel-scan order which changes k-means++ seeding. Harmless for a reported mean, NOT harmless for k-means: segment sizes moved by up to 45 users per run at a fixed seed. Guard is src.data.round_sig(..., sig=6), applied to every feature frame in 04 and MANDATORY for any notebook that re-derives these features. This is the concrete instance of the risk connect() flagged in the abstract.

NB00-NB03 HAVE NOT BEEN RUN END-TO-END IN ONE CONTINUOUS SESSION: nb03's Section 9 addendum was executed in a fresh kernel and spliced into the committed notebook. Every number reconciles on re-read, but a full clean re-execution of 00->03 in a single session is REQUIRED before nb09 if the README is going to claim reproducibility.

SEGMENT MEMBERSHIP IS NOT DURABLE: 04 fits clusters on Oct-Dec and scores Jan-Feb with the same centroids. The STRUCTURE reproduces (mix drift 1.53pp, independent-refit ARI 0.897) but only 56.8% of users stay in the same segment (Cohen's kappa 0.309, chance 37.5%). An equal-length window control (Nov-Dec vs Jan-Feb) reproduces this exactly, so it is behaviour, not an artefact. 08 must re-score segments at targeting time; a stored label misdirects ~2 users in 5.

BEHAVIOURAL CLUSTERS ARE A PARTITION OF A CONTINUUM, NOT DISCRETE TYPES: every silhouette across k=3..8 is below 0.25 (max 0.213 at k=3). k=4 is chosen on the elbow. The segments are descriptively useful and externally validated (4x spread in repeat rate, a variable never fitted on), but nothing downstream should treat them as latent classes.

RFM FREQUENCY IS DEGENERATE HERE: 77.5% of purchasers have exactly one order, so both F tercile boundaries fall on F=1 and F is scored on natural breaks (1/2/3+) instead. The RFM composite is effectively an R-and-M score, and R is near-identical to the churn flag (tercile boundary 41.11d vs threshold 42.2d). Any claim that RFM segments by loyalty at this retailer would be false.

BEHAVIOUR DOES NOT PROXY VALUE: across the 4 segments, eta-squared is 0.4594 on session depth (a fitted feature) but 0.0416 on median basket value (not fitted). All 6 pairwise basket-value comparisons are significant at p<1e-300 and none reaches a medium Cliff's delta. Segment membership must not be used as a stand-in for customer value in 08/09.
04 SEGMENTS PURCHASERS ONLY (109,732 of ~1.64M users). The ~1.53M non-purchasers are out of scope, so nothing in 04 supports a first-conversion (acquisition) recommendation.

CLUSTER FEATURES ARE NOT TENURE-NORMALISED: the Oct-Dec -> Jan-Feb drift is directional, toward the broad/deep segment, as browsing history accumulates. Part of what the clustering calls behaviour is tenure. 05 should either tenure-normalise or carry tenure alongside any segment feature.

RECALL CANNOT BE APPLIED WITHIN A RECENCY-DEFINED CELL (04 Section 9A, withdrawing 4C): recall 53.09% is a base-level property of the churn rule. Cells defined by recency have ~100% flagged by construction and cells defined by tenure<=30d have 0% by construction, so scaling either by 1/recall is invalid and points the wrong way. Use the base-level identity true_at_risk = correctly_flagged/recall only, and use segmentation.cross_tab.missed_churner_redistribution for where the missed actually sit.

THE CHURN RULE'S BLIND SPOT IS REPEAT BUYERS, NOT A BEHAVIOURAL SEGMENT (04 Section 9B): catch rate is flat at 51.7-55.5% across all four behavioural segments but falls to 36.9% for the high-value tercile. The driver is having a purchase cadence at all -- at-risk users with 2+ orders have a median personal gap of 14.1d, a third of the global 42.2d threshold, so the rule waits long past the point their habit broke. 05/06 should test a personalised (cadence-multiple) threshold; a different global K will not fix it.

CELL B1 IS LONG TENURE, NOT ENGAGEMENT (04 Section 9C, withdrawing Section 7 item 5): matching B1 against other Broad Deliberators on tenure-since-first-event does NOT close the engagement gap -- it widens on 4 of 5 metrics (Cliff's delta -0.31 -> -0.39 on assortment breadth, -0.31 -> -0.43 on sessions), narrows only slightly on session depth (-0.14 -> -0.12), and stays negative on all five both raw and matched. Per tenure-day B1 browses at 0.43x their rate. B1 is an activation-at-first-order population reached ~109 days late, not a re-engagement population. 08 should design on cell B3 instead, where the 42.2d window is still open.

04's TWO DETERMINISM GUARDS ARE NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT (05 Section 11): round_sig(sig=6) plus .sort_values('user_id') still left this notebook non-reproducible, and it failed its own zero-diff assertion on one cell of fo_price_vs_prior_mean out of 109,732. The parallel float wobble is ~1e-15 relative while round_sig snaps to a 1e-6 grid, so a value sitting within 1e-15 of a rounding boundary flips across it -- rounding makes the non-determinism RARE, not absent, which is a worse failure mode than an obvious one. A THIRD guard is required: SET threads=1 for the fetch itself (materialisations can stay parallel). Measured over 3 repeats per block: 48,738 differing cells sorted-only, 0 after 04's two guards, 0 with threads=1 before any rounding. Use src fetch_block().

FIRST-SESSION FEATURES MUST BE TRUNCATED AT t0 (05 Section 1A): 241,536 events sit in the first-order session AFTER the first order, across 11,704 users (10.7% of purchasers), including 24,625 purchase rows. 02's certified first_session_events is untruncated -- correct for 02's descriptive use, a leak as a feature. Untruncated it scores univariate AUC 0.5737 on repeat_purchase_30d against 0.5525 truncated.

04's cart_abandonment_rate CANNOT BE REBUILT IN A PRE-FIRST-ORDER WINDOW (05 Section 6A): there are zero purchases before t0 by construction, so the rate is a constant 1.0 for every user who has one. 04 computed it over full history, which for a post-t0 outcome is an outcome-window aggregate. Consequence beyond the one feature: segment_model.json cannot be applied faithfully to pre-t0 data -- one of its eight fitted features is degenerate there -- so 08's re-scoring at targeting time must use a window that contains at least one purchase, not a pre-first-order one.

PURCHASE CADENCE IS UNDEFINED AT A FIRST-ORDER ANCHOR (05 Section 7): 04 §9B's personalised-threshold recommendation cannot be tested as stated -- every user has exactly one order at t0, so the coverage gap is 100%, not the ~77% anticipated. 05 tested pre-t0 VISIT cadence instead: defined for 27.1% of users, personal median day-gap 3.5d against the 42.2d global rule (96.3% sit below it), LR chi2(1)=20.5 p=6.0e-06 but in-sample AUC gain only +0.0031. The test that would settle 04 §9B is a SECOND-ORDER anchor predicting the third order.

02's is_bulk_buyer IS A LEAKY FEATURE (05 Section 4C): it flags any order over 90.6 items across FULL history, so for 33 of the 143 flagged users the evidence post-dates their first order. Carried as a population flag (constraint 6 requires it) with model_eligible=False; first_order_is_bulk replaces it as the M1 feature.

05 PERSISTS ALL 109,732 PURCHASERS, NOT A PRE-FILTERED MODELLING SET: the three horizons have three eligible populations (D30 91,334, D60 71,727, D90 52,737), so 06 must subset on eligible_{h}d itself. 05's user-level eligibility rule differs from 02's cohort-level one by design and the cohort-eligible set is a strict subset of it; restricted to that subset, 05 reproduces 02's retention figures exactly.

UNIVARIATE CEILING IS AUC 0.6097 (05 Section 14B): across all 81 model-eligible features the best single column (pre_n_products) reaches 0.6097 against repeat_purchase_30d and the median reaches 0.5525; only 7 clear 0.60. Section 9C's 0.7386 is a LEAKAGE bound, not a signal bound, and sits 0.13 above the real ceiling -- do not quote it as evidence the table is informative. 06 must beat 0.6097 to justify a model over a one-feature rule, and must report PR-AUC/AP as the primary metric regardless.

bot_exclusion.metric: sessions per active day (distinct user_session count / distinct active-day count)
bot_exclusion.threshold_derivation: exact 99.9th percentile of the real distribution across all users; a generic Tukey far-outlier fence on raw session count was tested and rejected for over-flagging ordinary repeat shoppers (see notebook).
bot_exclusion.order_size_tail_correction: 00 claimed the order-size heavy tail was driven by the same high-volume user_ids; verified false -- zero overlap between the session-frequency bot list and the top mega-basket-order users, and the tail (max=429 items) is unchanged after bot exclusion. Treat as a separate, unresolved data issue for nb04/nb05.

bulk_buyer_segment.threshold_derivation: exact P99.9 of order size (quantile_cont), bot-excluded
bulk_buyer_segment.treatment: KEEP and flag as a named segment (is_bulk_buyer). Exclude from MEAN-based monetary metrics in 04/05 (AOV, mean CLV); report medians/winsorised means as headline.
bulk_buyer_segment.evidence: reseller/B2B signature: broad assortment, high volume, below-average unit price, one large haul, ~2x repeat rate of typical purchasers

retention_measured.definition_purchase: share of cohort placing >=1 further order within x days, in a session other than the first-order session
retention_measured.definition_activity: same window and session rule, any event type (superset of purchase)
retention_measured.eligibility_rule: cohort contributes to Dx only if its LAST joiner has >=x trailing days; ineligible cohorts are excluded, never zero-filled

compounding_vs_selection.implication_for_08: Do not assume an engineered 2nd purchase inherits the ~2x repeat rate; plan on the residual (1.27x), which is the part not explained by which buyers self-select into a fast 2nd purchase.

black_friday_cohort.naming_note: Renamed from 'promo_acquisition'. All detected spike days fall inside a single week, so this flag identifies the Black Friday cohort, not promotional acquisition generally. The old name overclaimed.
black_friday_cohort.spike_rule: day-level mean discount vs per-product median price exceeding median + 3*MAD of the daily series (derived from price dispersion only, no calendar input)
black_friday_cohort.primary_population: cohorts eligible at D90 (Oct+Nov), held fixed across D7..D90
black_friday_cohort.interpretation_limit: Associational, and about ONE trading week. Confounded with calendar position, merchandising and deal-seeking intent. Cannot justify a discounting decision on its own -- see 07 (Criteo) for randomised incrementality.

leakage_rules_for_05.rule: No feature may be derived from a cart-abandonment type whose definition references the outcome window. The 01/02 types (deferred_intent, substitution) require a purchase, and if that purchase is unbounded in time it can BE the predicted repeat purchase.
leakage_rules_for_05.evidence: Under the leaky spec deferred_intent scored OR=10.81 [10.29, 11.36]; with the classification window confined to events before the first order and the outcome measured strictly after it, the same type scores OR=0.78 [0.71, 0.85] -- below the baseline. The ranking inverts.
leakage_rules_for_05.safe_construction: Classify on events strictly before the first order (or a fixed first-k-day window); measure the outcome strictly after it; ensure every purchase a type definition references falls inside the classification window.
leakage_rules_for_05.what_survives: Abandonment VOLUME (log1p n_removals) remains predictive: OR=1.38 [1.35, 1.41]. Type does not.

spine_hypothesis_status.finding_name: SPINE-1: first-order value vs first-session depth is a dead heat, and both are weak
spine_hypothesis_status.original_claim: Repeat purchase is driven more by user behaviour and category/journey characteristics than by simple first-order value.
spine_hypothesis_status.verdict: First-order VALUE matches depth at D30 and exceeds it at D60 and D90. Behaviour does not beat first-order value. Both associations are weak (Cramer's V ~ 0.09-0.13), so neither is a strong standalone predictor of repeat purchase.
spine_hypothesis_status.replacement_framing: Repeat purchase and repeat engagement are separable problems at this retailer: by D90, 60% of purchasers return but only 27% buy again, a 33pp gap stable from D14 onward. Neither first-order value nor first-session depth predicts repeat purchase strongly, so the targeting question cannot be answered by propensity alone -- it requires estimating who would RESPOND to an intervention, which observational data cannot do (07/08).
spine_hypothesis_status.recorded_not_deleted: Kept as a named, dated falsification so 06/08 cannot silently re-adopt the original spine.

churn_definition.rule: A user is churned as of date D if (D - last order timestamp) >= 42.2 days, in exact elapsed seconds, over bot-excluded orders built with the certified order-reconstruction rule.

derivation.forward_method: max-separation cut (Youden's J) against a 56.9d forward window = 43.5d
derivation.why_this_is_the_certification: Two methods sharing no inputs land 1.3 days apart, and P75 scores J=19.63 against a ceiling of 19.90 -- it is on the plateau, not a slope.

churn_definition.reasoning: Certified on prevalence-free separation (Youden's J), NOT on misclassification cost. A cost sweep is degenerate here: at an 85% true-churn base rate, cost = c_FP*FP + c_FN*FN is minimised at K -> 0 for every R >= 0.47 and is strictly increasing in K from R >= 1.30, so across the whole economically sensible range it advises flagging everyone. Charging contact cost on all flagged users removes the degeneracy but breaks even between R=1.2 and 1.3, which nothing in the data pins down. Certifying a definition on intervention economics would make the churn rate a function of the marketing budget; the contact threshold is a separate decision and belongs in 08/09.
churn_definition.business_asymmetry_assumed: Symmetric per head: one missed churner costs about what one wasted contact costs (w=0.5). P75 wins only for w in [0.475, 0.525]; below that P85 wins, above it the 30-day rule and then the median win. The threshold is NOT robust to this assumption.

candidates_rejected.p95_87.3d: NOT VALIDATABLE. Needs 2K=174.6d of span; there are 152.0d. Its anchor falls 22 days before the first row of data, so zero users can be scored. Dropped, not weakly validated.
candidates_rejected.median_22d: J=13.72, flags 77% of the base -- close to flagging everyone.

naive_30d_contrast.direction: recency rules nest: the naive 30d rule flags a strict SUPERSET, 12,618 extra users, all with recency in [30, 42.2) days
naive_30d_contrast.honest_read: 30 days is a defensible operating point, not a catastrophic one -- 83% of its marginal contacts land on real churners. What deriving buys is a KNOWN position on the curve (J 17.02 vs 19.63 vs a ceiling of 19.90) and a priceable trade.

sensitivity_of_01_02_headlines.verdict: No conclusion from 01 or 02 reverses at any validatable threshold.
sensitivity_of_01_02_headlines.black_friday_gap: sign negative and CI excludes 0 in every measurable cell (range -7.83 to -2.46 pp); the 'WIDENS' trajectory is NOT assessable under P75/P85 because D7-D30 are unmeasurable
sensitivity_of_01_02_headlines.removal_volume_OR: first-order-anchored 1.37-1.44 at every K (02 committed 1.38); re-anchored to a calendar date it collapses to 1.03-1.14

persisted.labelled_panel: in_validation_panel == True (72,827 users) carries flagged_churned + true_churn_label

identification_status.claim: 42.2d is the centre of a 30-45d region; two independent methods agree there, but the estimate is robust to neither flag-date position nor cost asymmetry. ~9 months of history would identify it.
identification_status.why_an_operating_value_is_still_required: 04/05/06 must cut at one number or their results are not comparable. 42.2d is the best-supported point in the region; the region, not the decimal, is what the data supports.

evidence_against_precision.flag_date_drift: J-optimal K moves 43.5d -> 29.4d over 21 days of flag-date shift, tracking the lookback cap 95.1d -> 74.1d monotonically (Section 3D).
evidence_against_precision.cost_asymmetry_band: P75 wins only for recall weight w in [0.475, 0.525]; outside it P85 or the 30-day rule wins (Section 3C).
evidence_against_precision.taken_together: The estimate is robust to neither of the procedure's two free choices, so it is the value those choices produced rather than a property of the customers.

identification_status.what_survives: Every method tried lands in 30-45d (P75 42.2, forward-optimum at full lookback 43.5, forward-optimum at the earliest flag date 29.4). The J curve is flat across the region, so the choice within it costs little; the choice between it and 22d or 57d costs a lot (J 13.7 and 17.4 vs ~19.6-19.9).
identification_status.what_would_identify_it: ~9 months of history. With 270 days the threshold could be validated at a dozen flag dates each with a >150d lookback cap, and the drift would be measurable rather than confounded with left censoring.

addressable_population.where_the_missed_half_sits: All 28,986 missed churners have recency BELOW 42.2d at the flag date, by construction: median 23.7d, IQR [13.9, 34.6]. 36.1% sit in [30, 42.2) -- the band the naive 30-day rule would have caught, which is precisely the recall it buys and the false positives it pays for.
addressable_population.binding_rule_for_08_09: DO NOT treat the flagged population as the at-risk population. Sizing an intervention off 36,495 flagged users understates the at-risk base by 25,292 (41% short), while 3,694 of those flagged need no intervention. Any reach or ROI denominator built on the flagged count must be divided through by recall (53.09%), or it is wrong by roughly a factor of two.

base_rate_reconciliation.question: 03's Spec B gives a 56.9d forward window yet finds only 15.16% returning, against 02's D60 purchase retention of 21.08%. Is the 84.84% true-churn base rate fair?
base_rate_reconciliation.verdict: FAIR FOR THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS, and not comparable to 02's figure.
base_rate_reconciliation.anchor: 02 starts each user's clock at their own first order; 03 starts every user's clock on one calendar date. Return probability is a function of recency: the freshest stratum of 03's panel (recency <7d, i.e. 02's starting condition) returns at 27.42% over 56.9d, falling monotonically to 7.58% for the longest-lapsed band.
base_rate_reconciliation.composition: 02's population is a FLOW (new first-time buyers, all at recency 0); 03's is a STOCK (median recency 42.2d, only 4.73% within 7d of a purchase, 80.0% with one order). If the stock sat where 02's population starts, the churn base would be 72.58% rather than 84.84% -- the 12.26pp gap IS the recency mix.
base_rate_reconciliation.proof_of_agreement: Running 02's own first-order-anchored measure on 03's panel users reproduces 02 exactly: D30 14.08%, D60 21.08%. The notebooks do not disagree.
base_rate_reconciliation.left_censoring: Observable recency at F* is capped at 95.1d and users last active before 2019-10-01 are absent entirely, so the stock holds no long-dead customers. 84.84% therefore UNDER-states a mature retailer's point-in-time churn base.
base_rate_reconciliation.does_the_degeneracy_depend_on_it: NO, and this was the reason for checking. The cost model prefers flagging everyone once R exceeds the MAXIMUM LOCAL RETURN ODDS (0.378), not anything derived from the aggregate base rate; observed threshold 0.472 confirms the mechanism. On 02's own anchor the D60 odds are 0.267, still far below any realistic R, and reweighting the panel to 02's D60 rate moves the threshold only 0.472 -> 0.705. Section 3's argument is ANCHOR-INDEPENDENT and would not change if the base rate were 79%.

criteo_dataset.source_note: Criteo AI Lab's own Azure mirror. The canonical go.criteo.net link now 404s; a Hugging Face mirror (datasets/criteo/criteo-uplift) serves a byte-identical file (same 311,422,618-byte content-length) if this one moves.
criteo_dataset.schema_note: f0-f11 dense float features (anonymised); treatment 1/0; visit, conversion, exposure binary outcomes. No user id and no timestamp -- one row per randomised user.

naive_ate_unvalidated.warning: Raw difference in means, computed here ONLY to confirm the file is usable. It is NOT a result: 07 must derive the ATE properly with SRM and covariate-balance checks, CIs, and ITT vs TOT (exposure is post-randomisation, so conditioning on it breaks randomisation).

criteo_dataset.verified_by: scripted check outside the notebooks, after 03. 07 owns all analysis of this file.
criteo_dataset.why_it_is_here: REES46 has no randomised experiment (principle 10). Criteo is the genuine one (principle 11) and is what lets 07 show that risk-targeting != uplift-targeting -- the argument 03's cost-model degeneracy already points at from the observational side.

segmentation.snapshot_justification: DATA_END, the last event in the bot-excluded data. Forced by 03's churned_at_data_end being measured at exactly this instant -- Section 4 cross-tabs RFM recency against that flag, so they must share a clock.

population.note: Non-purchasers (~1.53M users) are OUT OF SCOPE. This notebook can size a second-order activation target; it says nothing about first conversion.

rfm.f_scoring: NATURAL BREAKS 1 / 2 / 3+ orders. NOT terciles -- both tercile boundaries fall on F=1, so a quantile cut on Frequency is impossible at this retailer.
rfm.recency_tercile_is_the_churn_flag: the fresher R boundary (41.11d) sits 1.09d from the certified churn threshold (42.2d); R_score and churned_at_data_end are near-duplicates, so 'high RFM AND at risk' is a contradiction and Section 4 uses a recency-free value_score = F_score + M_score instead.
rfm.value_score_definition: F_score + M_score, terciles Low=(2), Mid=(3,4), High=(5,6)
rfm.low_tercile_mechanism_correction: Section 4A claimed Low RFM requires R_score=1 (recency > 94.63d). FALSE: RFM_sum<=4 also admits (R=2,F=1,M=1), and 12,339 of 37,742 Low-RFM users have R_score=2. The conclusion (no Low-RFM user acquired within 30d) holds on the weaker premise that the minimum recency in the tercile is 41.12d > 30d. Corrected in Section 9D.

clustering.algorithm: k-means, k=4, seed 42, n_init=10, on 8 standardised features
clustering.transform: log1p on sessions_per_active_week/mean_session_depth/view_to_cart, then clip to per-feature [0.5, 99.5] percentiles, then z-score

features_dropped.mean_intersession_gap_d: undefined for 22,773 single-session purchasers (20.75%); requiring it would exclude the least-engaged fifth of the base, which is exactly 08's target. Retained as a profiling variable.
features_dropped.cart_to_purchase: Spearman rho = -0.936 with cart_abandonment_rate -- near rank-duplicates. The bounded one was kept.

determinism_guard.problem: DuckDB parallel float avg()/sum() reduce in physical scan order, so mean_price_pct_viewed, brand_entropy, category_entropy and mean_intersession_gap_d differ between two evaluations of the SAME query in one session (order 20-30k rows each, max |diff| ~9e-15; which rows differ is itself run-dependent). Cosmetic for a reported mean; NOT cosmetic for k-means, which reassigns boundary points on distance comparisons -- segment sizes moved by up to 45 users per run at a fixed seed before the guard was added.
determinism_guard.problem_2: fetchdf() returns rows in parallel-scan order, which is not stable across evaluations. Every statistic computed here is order-invariant, but k-means++ selects initial centres by sampling row INDICES, so a different row order seeds on different customers and converges to a neighbouring local optimum. Rounding alone did NOT fix reproducibility; this was the second cause.
determinism_guard.guard: BOTH are required: (1) src.data.round_sig(df, FLOAT_COLS, sig=6) on every feature frame immediately after fetch -- significant figures, not decimals, since the features span 1e-3 to 1e3; (2) .sort_values('user_id') on every feature frame, to make row order canonical.
determinism_guard.binding_on_05: Any notebook that re-derives these features MUST apply BOTH guards or it will not reproduce 04's segments.

clustering.leakage: NO abandonment TYPE features are used, per leakage_rules_for_05. Only cart_abandonment_rate, computed from products carted-and-not-bought inside the same window as every other feature. abandonment_user_types_leakage_safe.parquet was loaded and checked for coverage but deliberately not joined.

k_selection.method: elbow + silhouette over k=3..8, chosen BEFORE the stability test
k_selection.caveat: EVERY silhouette in the sweep is below 0.25. There are no well-separated natural groups in this feature space; k-means is partitioning a continuum. The segments are a useful description, NOT evidence that four discrete shopper types exist.

separation.verdict: Segments separate behaviour ~11x more strongly than spend. Every basket-value pair is significant and none reaches a medium Cliff's delta. Behavioural segmentation is NOT a proxy for monetary value here.

stability.design: fit on Oct-Dec, score Jan-Feb with the same clip bounds, scaler and centroids; k NOT re-tuned

equal_window_control.verdict: the instability is NOT a window-length artefact

stability.binding_rule_for_08_09: A stored cluster label is NOT a durable customer attribute. ~43% of users change segment within two months, so any campaign built on a stale segment list misdirects roughly two users in five. 08 must RE-SCORE membership at the moment of targeting using segment_model.json.
stability.known_confound: Drift is directional -- users migrate toward the broad/deep segment as history accumulates. None of the 8 features is tenure-normalised, so part of what the clustering calls behaviour is tenure.

cross_tab.interpretation: Weak-to-moderate. The two lenses are largely independent axes, which is what makes the cross-tab informative rather than a diagonal restatement of RFM.

A1.label: A1  High RFM x churn-like behaviour
A1.note: briefed cell: looks healthy on RFM, behaves like a non-returner

A2.label: A2  High VALUE x worst recency x churn-like behaviour
A2.note: the sharpest 08 target: proven spend, lapsed, and behaving like a one-off

A3.label: A3  High VALUE x worst recency (any behaviour)
A3.note: the classic high-value-at-risk cell, behaviour ignored

B1.label: B1  Low RFM x most-engaged behaviour
B1.note: engaged browsers written off by RFM as dead

B2.label: B2  Low/Mid VALUE x acquired within 30d
B2.note: low value only because they are new -- censored, not low-value

B3.label: B3  Low/Mid VALUE x acquired within 30d x engaged behaviour
B3.note: new AND behaving like the high-repeat segments: the best activation odds

cross_tab.headline: B1 (Low RFM x Broad Deliberators, n=10,982) is the largest disagreement cell, but Section 9C shows it is LONG TENURE rather than live engagement: matching on tenure widens its engagement gap against other Broad Deliberators on every metric, and per tenure-day it browses at 0.43x their rate. Treat it as activation-at-first-order, and prefer cell B3 (7,741 users, median tenure 15.5d) where the 42.2d window is still open.

disagreement_cells_recall_correction.what_was_wrong: Section 4C divided each cell's flagged count by recall (0.5309) to give implied_true_at_risk. Recall is a BASE-level property of the rule and cannot be applied inside a subgroup that is itself defined by recency. A2/A3 are R_score==1 cells where every member is flagged by construction, so scaling invents members the definition cannot hold; B2/B3 are tenure<=30d cells where flagged is 0 by construction, so scaling reports zero risk exactly where the missed churners live. The correction was anti-correlated with the truth and contradicted binding_constraint_from_03.structural_point.
disagreement_cells_recall_correction.correct_base_arithmetic: true_at_risk = correctly_flagged / recall = 32,801 / 0.5309 = 61,784, matching 03's 61,787. Dividing the FLAGGED count (36,495) by recall gives 68,742 and double-counts the 3,694 false positives.

missed_churner_redistribution.method: The 28,986 at-risk users the certified rule misses at F*=2020-01-04, cross-tabbed against behavioural segment and value tercile BOTH re-scored on pre-F* data (segment_model.json for clusters, orders<=F* for F and M). Snapshot-anchored labels agree on 96.3% of at-risk users, so the result is anchor-robust.
missed_churner_redistribution.finding_1: Behaviour does NOT predict visibility: the catch rate spans only 51.7-55.5% across the four segments, and the missed are spread roughly in proportion to segment size.
missed_churner_redistribution.finding_2: Value does: high-value at-risk users are caught only 36.9% of the time against 54.5% (Low) and 55.3% (Mid). 4,141 high-value at-risk users are invisible.
missed_churner_redistribution.mechanism: Repeat-buyer status, not value as such. At-risk users with 2+ orders are caught 37.7% vs 55.8% for one-timers. Their median personal inter-purchase gap is 13.8d = 0.33x the global 42.2d threshold, and 88.1% have a personal cadence below it, so the global rule waits far past the point at which their own habit was broken.
missed_churner_redistribution.recommendation_for_05_06: A personalised threshold (a multiple of each user's own cadence) rather than a different global K. Do not try to find the blind spot behaviourally -- it is not there.

b1_tenure_test.question: Is B1 engaged-but-written-off, or long-tenure-one-order?
b1_tenure_test.verdict: LONG TENURE. Section 7 item 5 is withdrawn.
b1_tenure_test.design: B1 vs other Broad Deliberators, direct standardisation over 9 deciles of tenure since FIRST EVENT, Cliff's delta within stratum weighted by B1's stratum sizes.
b1_tenure_test.gap_direction: Does not close. Widens on 4/5 metrics under tenure matching and stays negative on all 5 both raw and matched; narrows slightly only on session depth.
b1_tenure_test.implication_for_08: Not re-engagement -- there is no dormant engagement to revive. Activation at first order, and B1 is reached ~109 days too late. Cell B3 is the testable version of the same profile inside the open window.

binding_constraint_from_03.framing: FIRST-PURCHASE churn. At-risk cells here are ACTIVATION problems (get a 2nd order), not win-back problems.
binding_constraint_from_03.assumption: Recall was measured on 03's panel at F*=2020-01-04 and is ASSUMED to transfer to the 2020-02-29 snapshot. 03 showed the J-optimal threshold drifts with the flag date, so this is a first-order correction, not a precise one.
binding_constraint_from_03.structural_point: All missed churners have recency BELOW 42.2d, i.e. they score in the FRESHEST R tercile. The at-risk population is therefore NOT concentrated in the Low-RFM cells -- roughly half of it sits in cells that look healthy. A campaign sized off Low-RFM at-risk cells reaches at most half the at-risk base, and behaviour is the only lens here that can see the other half.

features.anchor: t0 = each user's first order timestamp, certified reconstruction rule
features.feature_window: event_time < t0, plus the first order's own purchase lines at exactly t0
features.outcome_window: orders with order_ts > t0 in a session other than the first-order session
features.eligibility_rule: t0 + horizon <= DATA_END in EXACT ELAPSED SECONDS; censored users excluded, never zero-filled
features.target_naming: repeat_purchase_{h}d. NOT churn -- D30 cannot carry a churn label under the certified 42.2d rule.

forbidden_list.F1_outcome_window_aggregate: any feature computed from events with event_time > t0
forbidden_list.F2_lifetime_or_recency: lifetime orders/spend, last-event recency, R/F/M, tenure-to-DATA_END
forbidden_list.F3_full_dataset_item_stats: product/category popularity or price stats over the full window

collinearity.handling: FLAGGED, NOT DROPPED. 06's logistic ladder must keep one per pair; LightGBM need not.

determinism.guards: THREE, all mandatory: SET threads=1 for the fetch, src.data.round_sig(sig=6), .sort_values('user_id'). 04 specified the last two; 05 found them insufficient.
determinism.why_04s_two_are_not_enough: the parallel float wobble is ~1e-15 relative and round_sig snaps to a 1e-6 grid, so a value whose 7th significant digit sits within 1e-15 of a rounding boundary flips ACROSS the grid. Rounding makes the non-determinism rare, not absent, which converts a reproducible failure into an intermittent one. It broke this notebook's first execution on one cell of fo_price_vs_prior_mean out of 109,732.
determinism.verified: two full builds through fetch_block(), 0 differing cells across all columns
determinism.cost: only the FETCH is single-threaded; materialisations stay on 6 threads. ~8s in total.
determinism.binding_on_06_and_later: call fetch_block() or reproduce all three guards.

leakage_verification.method_1_window_disjointness: row-level SQL: max feature-block offset 0s vs t0, min outcome offset 70s
leakage_verification.method_2_provenance_audit: every column declares its window; built-set and declared-set asserted equal
leakage_verification.method_3_screen_with_positive_controls: planted pure-outcome control AUC 0.9386; planted near-miss (02's untruncated first-session depth) AUC 0.5737 vs its truncated twin 0.5525; no shipped feature reaches 0.7386
leakage_verification.what_the_screen_cannot_do: univariate AUC cannot see a weak leak or an interaction leak; the load-bearing guarantees are methods 1 and 2

first_session_post_t0_leak.statement: 02's certified first_session_events is UNTRUNCATED and reads post-t0 events for 10.7% of purchasers, including purchase rows. Every M2 feature here is cut at t0. Measured cost of not truncating: univariate AUC 0.5737 -> 0.5525.

pre_window_abandonment_degeneracy.statement: There are ZERO purchases before t0, so 04's cart_abandonment_rate is a constant 1.0 in a strictly-pre-first-order window. 04 computed it over full history, which for a post-t0 outcome is an F1 violation. Replaced by pre_cart_not_in_first_order_rate.
pre_window_abandonment_degeneracy.consequence_for_segment_model: one of segment_model.json's eight fitted features is constant here, so the model cannot be applied faithfully to a pre-t0 window

purchase_cadence_undefined_at_t0.statement: 04 §9B asked 05/06 to test a personalised cadence threshold. At a first-order anchor every user has exactly one order, so purchase cadence is undefined for 100% of users, not the ~77% anticipated. Not a missingness problem -- the quantity does not exist yet.
purchase_cadence_undefined_at_t0.what_was_tested_instead: pre-t0 VISIT cadence (median gap between active days) and its lapse ratio

screen_result.verdict: significant and small. Carry it; do not build a targeting rule on it.

purchase_cadence_undefined_at_t0.the_test_that_would_settle_it: re-anchor on the SECOND order and predict the third. Purchase cadence is defined there. 06 or 08 owns that test.
purchase_cadence_undefined_at_t0.share_below_global_threshold_denominator: users with a DAY cadence defined (n=29,743), NOT all M4 rows

share_below_global_threshold_correction.cause: NaN-denominator bug. (M4.cad_day_median_gap_d < 42.2).mean() was taken over all 52,219 M4 rows, but only 29,743 have a day cadence; NaN < 42.2 is False, so the 22,476 users with no day cadence were counted as 'not below threshold' when they have no cadence at all.
share_below_global_threshold_correction.direction: the withdrawn figure UNDERSTATED the mismatch it was cited for
share_below_global_threshold_correction.conclusions_affected: none. Section 7's head-to-head and nested LR test never used this share. The corrected figure strengthens the finding and brings it in line with 04 §9B's 88.1% on purchase cadence, which at 54.8% looked like a different phenomenon.
share_below_global_threshold_correction.transcription_collision_checked: 04's addendum also reports a 96.3% (snapshot-label agreement on the 28,986 missed churners). Not the source: 05's value derives independently from 28,631/29,743 = 96.2613% and rounds to 96.3% by coincidence.

bulk_flag_is_leaky.statement: 33 of 02's 143 bulk buyers are flagged on an order that happens AFTER t0. is_bulk_buyer_fullhistory is carried as a population flag only; first_order_is_bulk is the model feature.

segment_rescoring.verdict: pre_segment is persisted but model_eligible=False. One of the eight fitted inputs is constant in a pre-t0 window, it is a lossy function of M3 features already in the table, and it inherits 04's membership instability. Kept as the reference implementation of the re-scoring 08 must do at targeting time.

binding_rules_for_06: Subset on eligible_{h}d. Never zero-fill a censored user -- an unobserved window is not a negative.
Split CHRONOLOGICALLY on first_ts, never randomly (CLAUDE.md principle 6).
Use only model_eligible == True columns. t0_calendar_day, trailing_days, is_bulk_buyer_fullhistory and pre_segment are in the file for diagnostics and must not be fitted on.
Encode fo_primary_brand / fo_primary_category INSIDE the training fold -- both are high-cardinality and a full-table encoding is an F3 violation.
Keep one feature per flagged collinear pair in the logistic ladder; LightGBM may keep both.
Do not impute. Every NULL has a named indicator (fs_has_pre_purchase_events, has_pre_t0_history, has_day_cadence, has_session_cadence).
The target is repeat_purchase_30d and must never be described as churn.

univariate_ceiling.scoring: direction-free ROC-AUC, max(a, 1-a); each feature on its own observed rows. The 3 non-numeric features are OOF target-encoded (5-fold stratified, seed 42).

complete_case.note: NOT a random subset -- requiring a cadence selects the most engaged fifth of the frame, which repeats at a higher rate, so every feature has less room to separate. Use it to confirm the ranking is not a coverage artefact, not as the operational ceiling.

univariate_ceiling.why_9C_could_not_tell_you_this: Section 9C's threshold (0.7386) was calibrated 0.20 below a planted outcome-window control so it would not flag honest signal as leakage. It is a bound on LEAKAGE and sits 0.13 above the real signal ceiling.
univariate_ceiling.binding_rule_for_06: A fitted model that does not clearly beat 0.6097 ROC-AUC is not worth shipping over a one-feature rule on pre_n_products. But ROC-AUC is the SECONDARY metric (principle 7): the decision criterion is PR-AUC / Average Precision against the 13.73% base rate, plus calibration and decile lift. Report this ceiling alongside them so the gain from modelling is legible.
